spans.text: Bremen, Germany.
Angelia's safe house.
Wanna bet?
20 minutes.
What are you talking about?
...They're guessing how long Ange will stay like this.
Huh...
I'm surprised you can tell what's going on.
This kind of nonsense is not uncommon with RPK.
It's not like we have anything to do.
Miss Ange has been like that for almost two hours.
She looks just like one of those somber Buddha statues in an old temple.
It's understandable.
We're in quite a bit of a pickle right now, after all.
A pickle?
Look at you, 15, quietly blending back into the background when the subject grows complex.
You need to be more of a team player, you know.
Thanks to our previous good deed of the day, the whole world now has their eyes on Griffin and Ange.
Everyone wants to know what happened in "that base" and the truth behind "that tech".
People of all kinds, nefarious or otherwise.
I'm sure we're being watched very closely.
Even the Stasi, who has so kindly prepared such lovely accommodation for us.
Hell knows what they're really up to.
In any case, this Mr. K does not strike me as a good man.
Indeed.
So given our circumstances, careful planning is certainly required before we begin our operation.
Going in blind without a clue will only land us in an even stickier situation.
Right now, Ange's every move is being watched. If she so much as buys an ice cream, a whole team of intelligence analysts will be there, looking for some kind of hidden significance.
Still, skulking in here and not doing a thing isn't a good idea either.
To our observers, our lack of action can also be perceived as a kind of action.
Who knows? This may actually make them even more uneasy.
But let's come back to our task at hand.
This is a really tough nut to crack.
Going out to buy a bottle of water and running into a dozen agents spying on us.
Having only ever watched people myself, I never thought I'd have the pleasure of being on the receiving end of this treatment.
"Abandon all hope,"
"Ye who enter here."
Or so they say.
Stop quoting poems out of context.
Come to think of it, how goes the "pest extermination"?
I removed twelve from the room and nine outside.
The signal transmission and audio pickup are top of the line—that's German engineering for you.
Maybe I should ask Mr. K to get me some more the next time I see him?
It's supposed to be a safe house... I did not expect to find so many bugs.
Which just goes to show that even those who look nice and friendly can be up to no good.
So have you disabled them all?
I've combed the whole place from floor to ceiling, but who knows?
It's not necessarily a bad thing even if you leave a bug or two.
If there's anything you want, just inform our eavesdropping friends.
They may have it delivered right away.
Hm, you have a point.
Uh, hello? You hear me?
Can I get a ham hock burger?
But look at it another way.
What we went through in Tallinn and Paldiski is our insurance and hole card.
It is the reason why Ange is granted a travel pass that gives her free passage.
...You are exactly right.
Oh, the Buddha is awake.
Besides, we've suffered great losses, and M4A1 is still MIA.
The Griffin Commander also needs time to recover.
We can't expect much help from them right now.
Or from the Stasi.
There is not a single person we can trust in this city.
I admire how effortlessly you just swanned your way into the conversation.
Not even Madam Ulrich?
She may actually be genuine in her desire to help us.
But her position makes it impossible for her act according to her own wishes.
What is it?
...The satellite phone just buzzed.
Give it to me.
What frequency?
Is it Havier?
That old fox wouldn't risk contacting us unless it's an emergency.
What's this about?
Patience. Decrypting this isn't exactly easy.
Hm...
Hoho... Interesting.
Stop being cryptic, or I'll let AK-12 handle all communications from now on.
Haha, if she's up to the task, I'm happy to be relieved of this duty.
Now don't be mad; it's good news.
Has anyone heard of the Flora Institute?
Sounds like a sweet factory.
What's with this institute?
The Commander has discovered some crates that might have originated from Germany.
Havier's people cross-referenced them with reports from other locations, and the contents are very likely to be Epiphylla filled with Collapse Fluid radiation particles.
As contamination sources, these crates have already wiped out several human settlements in the Yellow Zone.
I believe these coordinates that Havier just sent us are where the crates were dispatched from.
...Epiphylla.
Looks like our first clue has just presented itself.
And I was just saying we didn't have one.
Break time's over, 94.
Understood.
Knock knock.
Oh, my burger is here.
Well, this trip isn't looking so bad after all.
Stop fooling around. Disable the rest of the bugs and call Morridow.
Time to start our investigation.
